verdict_reason: The headline is exact: on 20 WikiText passages with gpt2 I re-implemented the HuggingFace strided protocol independently (window 1024, stride 512, blanket -100 on the overlap, sum of per-token cross entropies over the surviving mask) and got PPL 20.647981295676 over 1720 scored targets against BLME's 20.647978516549 over the same 1720 -- relative 1.35e-07. I CONFIRM codex's bits_per_byte defect but not its severity. utils.py:857-873 splits a shared offset span EVENLY among the tokens that share it, which is total-preserving but not per-token exact: for gpt2 on '\U0001F600b' the byte-BPE ownership is [3, 1, 1] and BLME assigns [2.0, 2.0, 1.0], so scoring all-but-the-first counts 3 bytes instead of 2 (-33.3%); pythia-70m is [2,1,1,1] vs [1.333,1.333,1.333,1.0], 3 vs 3.667 (-18.2%). The error is bounded by the bytes of the multi-token characters straddling the scored-set BOUNDARY plus the int(round()) of a fractional total, which is why it is 0 bytes on the shipped corpus and 1 byte in 1,295,023 (7.7e-7) on WikiText-2 non-overlap. On 'a\u2011b', which has a multi-token character in the interior, exact and BLME agree at 4 bytes exactly.
comparable_reason: ppl_overall is a token-level quantity and is therefore a function of the tokenizer's granularity, not only of the model: at IDENTICAL source likelihood, grouping 1/2/4 source bytes per token moves PPL by 8x. bits_per_byte removes exactly that dependence and is the right cross-model column; the residual objection to it is the byte-attribution error above, which is 7.7e-7 on real text. The deeper caveat is not comparability but CATEGORY: this is a likelihood/capability measure, so it belongs on the dependent-variable side of this study, not among the structural predictors. ppl_rare / ppl_freq are additionally tokenizer-dependent through the bucket construction (frequency ties are broken by token ID at perplexity.py:57), so their ratio is comparable only between models sharing a tokenizer.
normalized_variant: bits_per_byte (and bits_per_char); _meta_bits_per_byte_lower_bound when offsets are unavailable
github_reason: I re-implemented and executed the HF guide's strided loop locally against BLME on gpt2 over the same joined stream: identical scored-target count (1720) and PPL agreeing to 1.35e-7. I did NOT fetch or execute lm-eval itself this round; I instead reconstructed exact byte-BPE ownership from the GPT-2/NeoX byte_to_unicode table and compared it token-by-token against BLME's offset partition, which is the actual disputed quantity. Neither reference implements BLME's 'scored subset of a strided stream' byte denominator -- lm-eval's bits_per_byte divides a whole-document loglikelihood by the whole document's UTF-8 length -- so no reference is an oracle for this specific number.
paper_reason: There is no source paper for this task; the reproducible anchors are the protocol's own. (a) The HF guide's own claim -- that the strided protocol is what published perplexities use and that a naive per-document reduction is much worse -- reproduces here: ppl_overall 20.647979 (strided) vs ppl_overall_perdoc 45.534437 on the same 20 passages, a 2.2x gap that the task correctly reports under two separate names. (b) The analytic anchor for BPB: a uniform binary one-byte-per-symbol source has entropy exactly 1 bit/byte, and BLME returns 1.000000003 (2.7e-9). GPT-2's own Table 3 WikiText-2 figure of 29.41 is not reproducible here because it uses invertible detokenisation, and the guide's worked 19.44/16.44 examples use gpt2-large.
confounds_reason: By construction rather than by accident: perplexity IS the training objective, so it tracks capability and therefore parameter count directly. Two mechanisms measured here: (a) raw PPL moves 8x under pure tokenizer regrouping at fixed source likelihood, so it is partly a tokenizer statistic; (b) the frequency buckets are ID-tie-broken, so ppl_rare/ppl_freq are not tokenizer-independent strata. bits_per_byte removes (a). None of this makes the number wrong -- it makes it a dependent variable. normalization.is_feature accepts all eight public numeric outputs, which puts a likelihood measure into a structural feature matrix.
defects: CODE / BYTE ATTRIBUTION LABELLED EXACT WHEN IT IS NOT (utils.py:857-873, `_byte_exact = True` at :880). Tokens sharing a character-offset span split that span's bytes evenly rather than by their true byte-BPE ownership. Measured on gpt2 '\U0001F600b': exact widths [3,1,1], BLME [2.0,2.0,1.0]; the scored-set denominator is 3 instead of 2, a -33.3% BPB error on that corpus. Interior multi-token characters are unaffected (both give 4 on 'a\u2011b') because the halves cancel; only a scored-set boundary that cuts a character, plus the int(round()) of the fractional total, leaks -- 1 byte in 1,295,023 on WikiText-2 non-overlap, 0 on the shipped 200-passage corpus. Exact ownership IS recoverable from the byte_to_unicode table (I did it in ~10 lines for both gpt2 and pythia), so the approximation is not forced.

PROTOCOL: frequency-bucket ties are broken by token ID (perplexity.py:57, np.lexsort((observed_ids, observed_counts))). This is deterministic and documented, but it means ppl_rare and ppl_freq are not purely frequency strata -- among equally frequent types, membership is decided by an arbitrary vocabulary index.

CATEGORY / STUDY DESIGN: normalization.is_feature accepts ppl_overall, ppl_rare, ppl_freq, bits_per_byte and the rest. A cross-entropy measure is the study's dependent variable, not a structural predictor; admitting it to the feature matrix makes 'metrics predict capability beyond scale' partly circular. SIZE_LINKED_BY_MEANING also names a key, geometry_perplexity.perplexity, that this task never emits.

PROTOCOL / CONFIG: defaults.yaml num_samples=100 with a study override of 200; the manuscript's methodology section specifies >=64 tokens and 128-token truncation while the shipped corpus builder uses >=50 characters and untruncated joined text. Reconcile the two; this changes which passages are scored, not how they are scored.

GOOD PRACTICE WORTH KEEPING: the offset-less branch refuses to publish a fabricated denominator and emits _meta_bits_per_byte_lower_bound instead, and ppl_overall goes NaN rather than silently switching to the per-document protocol when the strided pass fails. Both were correct on inspection.
fix: Replace the even split in utils.py:857-873 with exact byte-BPE ownership: map each token string through the tokenizer's byte_decoder (or byte_to_unicode inverse) to get its true byte width, verify that the widths concatenate to the source, and sum only the widths of scored targets. That removes the fractional accumulation and the int(round()) entirely, and makes '\U0001F600b' give 2 instead of 3. Where the concatenation check fails (added tokens, non-byte-level tokenizers), withhold bits_per_byte and emit the existing _meta_ bound rather than setting _byte_exact = True. Independently, either exclude geometry_perplexity from the structural feature matrix in normalization.py or mark its outputs explicitly as dependent variables, and fix the SIZE_LINKED_BY_MEANING entry to name an emitted key.
